This worksheet works on created a corrected chlorophyll fluorometer time-series through comparison with discrete chlorophyll samples.

```{r}
#Upload packages
library(tidyverse) #wrangling
library(here) #file management
library(readxl) #reading excel files
library(lubridate) #working with dates and time
library(ggsci)

```

```{r}
t <- read_csv(here("files", "8_binAvg-1749754037389.csv")) 

q <- read_csv(here("outputs", "flagged_turbidity_casts.csv")) 

```

```{r}
#Renaming columns so that they are easier to work with
t1 <- t %>% 
  select(castpk = `Cast PK`,
         ctd_num = `CTD serial number`,
         station = Station,
         time = `Measurement time`,
         pres = `Pressure (dbar)`,
         t = `Turbidity (FTU)`,
         t_flag = `Turbidity flag`) %>% 
  filter(t_flag == "null") %>% 
  mutate(date = date(time))

#Determining number of casts
num_cast <- t1 %>% 
  select(castpk) %>% 
  distinct()

#Using the results of the QC script to filter out bad casts.
t2 <- t1 %>% 
  left_join(q) %>% 
  filter(!flag_type == "bad_cast")
```

```{r}
#Selecting cast 10 minimum values and calculating mean and standard deviation of minimum values. Removing surface data as sometimes there are downspikes at the surface
dark_10 <- t2 %>%
  filter(pres > 10) %>% 
  group_by(castpk, date, ctd_num) %>% 
  slice_min(t, n = 10, with_ties = F) %>% 
  summarise(min_mean = mean(t),
            min_std = sd(t),
            n = n()) %>% 
  ungroup()

#Filtering profiles with high dark value standard deviations - none exist anymore after bad casts were removed.
check_dev <- dark_10 %>% 
  filter(min_std > 0.1)

#Plotting casts with high dark value standard deviations
# t2 %>% 
#   filter(castpk %in% check_dev$castpk) %>% 
#   ggplot(aes(x = t, y = pres)) +
#   geom_line(orientation = "y") +
#   scale_y_reverse() +
#   facet_grid(~castpk, scales = "free")
```
```{r}
#removing casts with high dark value standard deviations from the main data sheet
t3 <- t2 %>% 
  # filter(!castpk %in% check_dev$castpk) %>% 
  left_join(dark_10)
```

```{r}
#Plotting dark values by sensor
dark_10 %>% 
  filter(!castpk %in% check_dev$castpk) %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = date, y = min_mean, color = as.factor(ctd_num))) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  facet_grid(ctd_num~., scales = "free_y") +
  scale_color_npg() +
  theme_bw()

#Some massive differences especially 18066 in 2024 - why?
```
```{r}
t3 %>% 
  mutate(year = year(date)) %>% 
  filter(year == 2014 & ctd_num == 18066 & min_mean < 1) %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = t, y = pres)) +
  geom_line(orientation = "y") +
  scale_y_reverse() +
  facet_wrap(~castpk, scales = "free")

#Clearly some issues here with this sensor - I think I need to go through and visually inspect - not much way around it.
```

```{r}
#For now, just going to subtract the dark value from each cast.
t3 <- t3 %>% 
  mutate(t_cor = t - min_mean)
```

```{r}
t3 %>% 
  mutate(year = year(date),
         month = month(date)) %>%
  filter(pres == 5 | pres == 10 | pres == 30) %>% 
  group_by(month, pres) %>% 
  summarise(t_cor = mean(t_cor)) %>% 
  ungroup() %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = month, y = t_cor, color = as.factor(pres))) +
  geom_line(size = 2)
```

```{r}
t3 %>% 
  mutate(year = year(date),
         month = month(date)) %>%
  filter(month == 7 & pres > 4 & station == "KC10") %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = t_cor, y = pres)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.1) +
  geom_smooth(orientation = "y", span = 0.1) +
  scale_y_reverse() +
  facet_wrap(~year) +
  theme_bw()
    

```
